mainEntity.name: Do I need an expensive camera or lens?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Any DSLR or mirrorless camera with manual exposure modes is perfect — it doesn't need to be new or expensive. Ideally bring a zoom (50mm+) or a 50mm prime, but the kit lens you already have is a fine place to start.

mainEntity.name: Will there be a model to photograph?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We provide the models for the practical session, so you get to photograph a real subject under studio lighting with guidance — rather than just talking theory.

mainEntity.name: I'm a complete beginner — will I be out of my depth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not at all. The course assumes only a basic understanding of exposure and builds from there. With a maximum of four people there's time for questions and individual help, and there's genuinely no such thing as a silly question here.
It's a full day, roughly 9am to 5pm, with about an hour for lunch. You'll cover lighting, settings, composition and posing, with a hands-on practical session photographing a model.

mainEntity.name: Where is it held and is there parking?

acceptedAnswer.text: The course runs at our studio at 17A Spon Street, Coventry, CV1 3BA. Parking is Pay & Display, or the Skydome Multi-Storey Car Park (15 Croft Road, CV1 3LD) is a short walk away.

mainEntity.name: Can a friend or partner come along to watch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Places are limited to four participants to keep the day personal, so it's for booked participants only rather than observers. If a friend or partner would also like to learn, they're very welcome to book their own place.
Yes — younger photographers are welcome, but anyone under 18 must be accompanied by a paying adult on the course.
Not as standard, but one is available on request — an informal acknowledgement of completing your portrait photography training.

mainEntity.name: What if no dates are listed right now?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you don't see a date to book, dates for the next course haven't been scheduled yet. The quickest option is Alan's private 1-2-1 package, which covers the same material around your own schedule — or get in touch to be told when the next date is set.

mainEntity.name: What can I do after the portrait course?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most people add the Lightroom photo editing course to develop their images, or continue with monthly mentoring or 1-2-1 lessons. If you're aiming higher, there's also RPS distinction support.

mainEntity.name: What happens if a course can't run?

acceptedAnswer.text: On the rare occasion a course can't go ahead, you'll be offered an alternative date or a credit.
